messages:
Ashley Kim: quick sync — I'm trying to close the active/active degradation contract doc. question: do we treat cross-region fallback as an opt-in per-tenant policy (tenant-level consent bit) or a per-request hint? i.e., should the proxy be allowed to route outside the residency region automatically when deg mode hits, or must the control-plane authorize fallback? :thinking:
Matt O'Connor: i'd push for a per-tenant flag. making this per-request will cause messy client-side churn and hard-to-debug behavior. header like `X-Residency-Fallback: allow` seems reasonable.
Sara Li (Legal): legal view: we need explicit opt-in and audit trail. for EU-residency tenants, fallback should be disabled by default. if a tenant opts in, we need acceptance logging + versioned consent (who/when). fallback-by-default is a compliance risk. :warning:
Leo Martinez: implementation notes from runtime: if we add `X-Residency-Fallback`, proxy logic is small but KV cache semantics change. fallback requests will hit a different region's cache and KV TTLs could diverge. also session affinity: if client sticks to region A, then fallback to B could see cold kv and different model variant. we should define expectations in the contract.
Olivia Park: ops perspective — cost spike concern. if many tenants allow fallback, traffic could shift to cheaper regions and blow budgets. need rate limits or budget windows for cross-region deg fallback. also want telemetry counters + sampling traces.
Ashley Kim: agreed on telemetry. proposal: three-tier residency mode per-tenant: `strict` (no fallback), `hinted` (proxy may attempt local then fallback with header), `open` (system can route based on SLO/cost). default is `strict` for regulated regions.
Matt O'Connor: API shim suggestion: expose `/v1/tenants/{id}/routing-config` with `residency_mode: [strict|hinted|open]` and `fallback_audit: boolean`. control plane enforces default and records consent.
Sara Li (Legal): that's acceptable if the API forces explicit toggle and stores timestamped consent. also require purge policy description for any data transferred under fallback. who owns that policy? product + legal.
Leo Martinez: on the runtime hook: two places to enforce — proxy (fast path) and control-plane sidecar (policy store). prefer proxy-enforced decision for latency but proxy must consult a cached policy with TTL and fallback to control plane on miss. that yields simpler rollbacks.
Olivia Park: can we get a safe rollout matrix? something like: 1) internal-only tenants in canary, 2) 10% of traffic with `hinted`, 3) full opt-in after 2 weeks of telemetry. include cost/traces gating.
Ashley Kim: yea — also need a doc snippet for SLO carve-outs when fallback occurs. e.g., requests served from secondary region get a different latency SLO and cost attribution tag.
Matt O'Connor: small config example for clients/ops:
```
residency_mode: hinted
fallback_header: X-Residency-Fallback: allow
fallback_budget_per_hour: 1e6_tokens
```
Leo Martinez: follow-up infra tasks: 1) add policy cache to proxy (expiry 30s), 2) telemetry counters: fallback_attempts, fallback_successes, fallback_latency_bucket, 3) KV tag to indicate origin-region for cache entries.
Sara Li (Legal): add audit events: `fallback_requested`, `fallback_executed`, `consent_changed`. store user id for consent changes. encryption-at-rest requirements unchanged but add access log retention note.
Olivia Park: ops runbook snippet: if fallback_attempts > 1% and cost delta > X, auto-scale down fallback weight and alert oncall. also add quick rollback CLI: `redwood routing disable-fallback tenant-id`.
eng-oncall-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment to `canary-proxy` finished — version v2.17.4. no errors in 10m.
Ashley Kim: next action items: Matt to draft tenant API + default policy, Leo to write proxy policy-cache PR, Olivia to produce rollout matrix and cost gate, Sara to write audit field reqs. i'll stitch into the contract doc and propose for arch review next Tue. thanks everyone :)
